### Load tidyverse, lubridate and data
```{R}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)

raw <- read.csv("data/salary_data_raw.csv")

raw
```

### Clean inconsistent result 
```{R}
clean <- raw %>%
  mutate(
    Salary = recode(
      Salary,
      "70,000" = "70000",  
      "72,000" = "72000",
      "65k"    = "65000"
    ),
    Salary = as.numeric(Salary),
    Date.of.employment = recode(
      Date.of.employment,
      "Feb 1, 2026"     = "1/02/2026", 
      "2 days ago"      = "23/08/2026", 
      "1/02/2000 10:00" = "1/02/2000"
    ),
    Date.of.employment = dmy(Date.of.employment)
  )

clean
```

## Dealing with NA value 
### Approach 1 — Drop the missing values
```{R}
clean

cleanclean_drop <- clean %>%
  drop_na(Salary)

clean_drop
```

### Approach 2 — Replace with the mean
```{R}
clean_mean <- clean %>%
  mutate(
    Salary = ifelse(
      is.na(Salary),
      mean(Salary, na.rm = TRUE),
      Salary
    )
  )

clean_mean
```

### Approach 3 — Rule-based imputation
```{R}
clean %>%
  group_by(City) %>%
  summarise(city_median = mean(Salary, na.rm = TRUE))

clean_rule <- clean %>%
  mutate(Salary = ifelse(is.na(Salary), 64750, Salary))

clean_rule
```

### Approach 4 — Linear regression imputation
```{R}
sal_lm <- lm(Salary ~ Age + City, data = clean)

clean_lm <- clean %>%
  mutate(
    Salary = ifelse(
      is.na(Salary),
      predict(sal_lm, new_data = clean),
      Salary
    )
  )

clean_lm
```
